preregistered.primary: H accuracy under identity-primary exceeds coverage-only on held-out isolates
preregistered.falsified_if: H gain <= 0, or resolution changes materially

discovery.note: UNBLINDED -- the fix was chosen after seeing this cohort's failures

why: identity-primary beats coverage-only by +0.1057 on isolates the fix was never chosen from, clearing the pre-registered +0.05 bar.
honest_limits: Both rules are scored from ONE blastn pass per isolate, so the only difference is the sort key -- but that also means shared blast parameters/DB limits affect both equally.
Disjointness is by accession against the discovery checkpoint; two accessions could still be near-identical genomes, so this is held-out by ISOLATE, not by lineage.
Still no in-silico incumbent for E. coli (PD leaves computed_types null), so the ABSOLUTE accuracy remains weakly anchored; the RULE COMPARISON is what this run tests.
O-only labels score the O axis alone -- the axes have different denominators.

net_effect.note: the O axis is very slightly WORSE under identity-primary (-0.0086, 2 isolates). Reported rather than buried: the net is strongly positive but the trade-off is real.

regression_from_discovery.interpretation: the gain shrank on held-out isolates exactly as an UNBLINDED choice predicts. This CONFIRMS the discovery caveat rather than undermining it -- quote the held-out +0.106, not the discovery +0.155.

secondary_prediction_outcome.why_it_matters: the mechanism claim was that the rule picks WHICH allele wins, not WHETHER one does. An exactly-zero no_call delta on 250 isolates is direct corroboration of that mechanism, not just of the effect.
